analysis: Before-change local call timings identify full binding projection and the 178-row directory projection as the largest local facade reads. persona.get_surface_status reads its provider once; runtime.get_surface_status is called twice (scope and dataset_source), both reuse the same request owner read. These supplied in-memory rows do not reproduce the hosted network latency; no new hosted timings are claimed.

Initial binding, telemetry and monitoring reads now overlap in the existing 16-worker owner executor. Unique admitted strategy details and latest outcome reads overlap in a second batch, joined before projection. The deterministic barrier regressions prove overlap without a wall-clock performance threshold.

Canonical get_rollbacks facade calls decrease from 3 to 1 per request by reading the already tenant-verified collection once and indexing by runtime. This reduces facade/filter work; the lower Governance owner HTTP collection was already request-cached, so this is not a claim of 3 to 1 HTTP/SQL calls. Runtime-only injected get_rollbacks contracts retain the existing behavior.

Both routes retain 1 binding list, 1 telemetry list, 1 monitoring list, 1 persona directory list, 1 persona status and 2 runtime statuses; the persona and runtime providers are each invoked once. Both retain 3 bounded current strategy reads, 3 pure baseline comparisons and no drift list or per-row telemetry/monitoring/baseline getter. Pulse retains 3 indexed latest journey pages; rankings retains 0.

Scale regression holds active facts constant and increases retired-marked bindings 113 to 2260 and telemetry rows 3 to 60. Every observed call count stays identical and both full response payloads equal the saved before-change payloads. No fixture wall-clock speedup is claimed: dispatch overhead makes these memory-only calls slower locally; the improvement targets serialized remote waits and repeated facade work.

The frozen before_payloads were captured before changing service.py, at anchor 18e55d9db, using the same real-port fixture and fixed snapshot. Full dict/list equality compares all fields, arrays, nulls and surface metadata, including a nonempty rollback summary. Pulse and rankings each exercise their existing outcome behavior.
